correctness.rationale: The rooted star P_n has 2^n leaf upsets and one top. A nucleus j has leaf behavior U union (L\A) determined from j(empty), since meet preservation with singleton leaves prohibits introducing an A-leaf not in U. The filter of inputs whose images contain the root is principal; its generator is either top (flag 1) or exactly A (flag 0), the latter forced by idempotence. Thus exactly 2^(n+1) maps J_(a,A). For two maps leaf components of compositions coincide; root membership in mixed flags compares A cap B subset U with A subset U, giving precisely the inclusion criterion. The families F_I are maximal by inserting all eligible subsets and supersets. Per-leaf binary incidence for h flag-zero and k-h flag-one tuple entries gives 2^h+2^(k-h)-1 choices, independent across leaves, proving the all-n,k spectrum and probability. A fresh evaluator computed every ordered commuting pair for n=1..4 (14,50,182,674) using pointwise maps rather than the case proof; the symbolic proof handles all n and k.
residual_risks: Finite independent checks only corroborate stated finite domains; universal assertion follows symbolic proof and stated dependencies.

value.rationale: The exact compatibility graph, maximal-clique stratification indexed by I, all-arity count and asymptotic commutation probability give a natural structural profile of meet-preserving closure operations on the simplest nonchain distributive lattices. These data are not textbook consequences of counting single nuclei and plausibly useful when studying commuting localizations or simultaneous closure operations. Not claimed for arbitrary posets.
